content: Nature has given men one tongue but two ears, that we may hear from others twice as much as we speak.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Loneliness is the painful ache of feeling incomplete, while solitude is the rich discovery of your own inner presence. In a world full of constant stimulation and notifications, being alone with your thoughts can feel intimidating.

Across his life and work, Marcus Aurelius saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Yet silence is the only space where you can hear what your life is actually trying to say to you. When you make peace with quiet, you stop running to distractions to save you from yourself.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
